questions.prompt: In the trace, a request has max_tokens 16000. Why does DeepSeek never receive it?
options: The timing listener did not call next()
The kernel rejects any request above 8192 tokens
The budget listener returned an error without calling next(), so the inner work never ran
The loop checks max_tokens before sending
questions.explanation: The chain reaches the inner work only through next(). Budget returned its error instead, so inner() never ran and the error went back through timing.

questions.prompt: A logging listener on a waterfall prints the request and returns nothing, without calling next(). What happens?
options: The request is sent, and the log is printed
The kernel calls next() for it
The work stops silently, and the result is undefined
questions.explanation: Not calling next() stops the chain. A listener that only watches must call next() once and return what it gives back.

questions.prompt: Why does the timing listener print a time for the refused request too?
options: It runs before budget, so its next() returns budget's error and it continues after that
The kernel calls every listener twice
Budget calls timing when it refuses
questions.explanation: Timing is the outer layer. Its next() call returns whatever the inner layers return, here the error, and then the rest of its code runs.
